test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is the correct expression for power developed at the crankshaft in terms of mechanical efficiency?

Consider BP - brake power, IP - Indicated power
solution:
The correct answer is __BP = IP × Mechanical efficiency__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mechanical efficiency__ is the ratio of brake power (BP) to indicated power (IP).
 
• It represents the efficiency with which the engine converts the indicated power into usable brake power.
 
• The formula for brake power is given as **BP = IP × Mechanical efficiency**.
 
• Mechanical efficiency accounts for losses such as friction and other resistances in the engine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake Power (BP):**

 
 
• It is the usable power delivered by the crankshaft of an engine.
 
• It is measured using a dynamometer.
 
 
 
• **Indicated Power (IP):**
 
 
• It is the power developed inside the engine cylinder by the combustion of fuel.
 
• It is always higher than brake power due to frictional and other losses.
 
 
 
• **Efficiency:**
 
 
• Mechanical efficiency is one of the key performance indicators for engines.
 
• Higher mechanical efficiency indicates better utilization of the indicated power.
